headline: Approved $5.7 million police body camera contract, several service contracts, and final passage of Video Display Signs Overlay District ordinance.
summary: The board appointed two new cemetery trustees and approved several contracts, including body-worn cameras, special event software, landfill gas monitoring, and flow monitoring. It gave final passage to resolutions R-26-053 through R-26-056, adopted Ordinance O-26-022 creating the Video Display Signs Overlay District, and passed R-26-049 establishing a Homeless Services Gap Analysis Committee after two amendments failed. New items on PFAS removal funding and stop signs at French and Abbott Streets were introduced and referred to committee.
decisions: Appointed Jamie Viveiros and Gerry Reppucci as new Trustees of Woodlawn & Pinewood Cemeteries.
Accepted written communications and placed them on file.
Approved purchase of Axon body-worn, fleet, and interview room camera system for up to $5,699,999.83.
Approved a three-year special event permitting software contract with Event Approvals, Inc. for up to $117,000, 13-1.
Approved landfill gas telemetry monitoring contract with Sanborn, Head & Associates for up to $87,750.
Approved Amendment #1 with ADS Environmental Services, LLC for collection system flow monitoring, up to $46,500.
Approved a license agreement with Harbor Care for a resource center proof of concept, 13-0 with one abstention.
Accepted the Petition for Street Acceptance for Juliana Avenue, referred it to the Committee on Infrastructure, and scheduled a public hearing for October 14, 2026.

Accepted the Mayor's appointments to the Arts Commission, Business and Industrial Development Authority, and Electric Aggregation Committee, and referred them to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee.
Gave final passage to R-26-053, increasing annual road and highway funding from motor vehicle permit fees from $1,000,000 to $2,000,000.
Gave final passage to R-26-054, authorizing Pennichuck Corporation to renew and extend its line of credit with TD Bank, N.A.
Gave final passage to R-26-055, transferring $85,100 into Department 159 Hydrants – Fire Protection, Account 54835, 13-1.
Gave final passage to R-26-056, transferring $10,500 within Department 157 Citywide Communications.
Gave final passage to O-26-022, establishing the Video Display Signs Overlay District, 9-5.
Voted to remove Resolution R-26-049 from the table, 14-0.
Failed a motion to amend Section D of R-26-049 regarding the gap analysis report timeline and disbanding language, 2-12.
Failed a motion to amend Section (b)1 of R-26-049 regarding committee membership, 4-10.
Gave final passage to R-26-049, establishing a Homeless Services Gap Analysis Committee, 12-1.
Gave R-26-057 its first reading, assigned it to the Budget Review Committee and Board of Public Works, and scheduled a special public hearing for September 28, 2026.
Gave O-26-024 its first reading and assigned it to the Committee on Infrastructure and City Engineer for stop signs at French Street and Abbott Street.
